key_insight: Hybrid Reasoning Agents let an AI reason internally in a latent space when speed and efficiency matter, then switch back to text when it needs to use tools or communicate externally. This creates a single agent that can think beyond language without losing the flexibility of language-based interaction.
problem_solved: Current LLM agents are forced to reason and act through text, which is slow and inefficient, while latent reasoning is efficient but usually cannot directly access tools or provide transparent outputs. This paper addresses the gap by unifying both modes in one agent.
method: Introduce a hybrid agent architecture that dynamically switches between latent reasoning and text-based reasoning during one generation process.
Use latent space for internal computation and planning, while using text tokens for tool use, interaction, and interpretable outputs.
Coordinate both modes so the agent can reason efficiently without sacrificing external action capability or transparency.
impact: This approach could make AI agents more efficient, flexible, and practical for real-world workflows where both deep internal reasoning and clear external communication are needed. For practitioners, it offers a path toward agents that are faster than pure text-based systems yet still usable in tool-rich environments.
